title: Devotional Journal for Women: Free Page and 40 Prompts
description: A devotional journal for women: a free page to fill in and print, a 7 day plan, 40 prompts for busy seasons, a filled example, and ideas for men too.
intro: A **devotional journal for women** gives you a simple page for your quiet time: a verse, what it shows you about God, how it touches your life this week, and a prayer. Start with the free page below. It takes about ten minutes and you can print it or save it as a PDF.

fields.label: What God is like in this passage
Where this meets my life right now
fields.hint: At home, at work, in my heart

fields.label: One thing I will do or believe today

sections.h2: What a devotional journal for women is

blocks.p: A devotional journal is the page you write on during your time with God. You read a short passage, think about it, and respond in writing. A devotional journal for women shapes those questions around the real life of a woman: the people she cares for, the roles she carries, and the quiet battles she does not always talk about.

It is not a test of how spiritual you are. Some days you will write a full page. Some days you will write one line at a red light before school pickup. Both count. For the general method, see our [devotional journal](/devotional-journal/) guide.

sections.h2: A 7 day devotional journal plan for busy women

blocks.p: Use one passage for the whole week. Spend about ten minutes a day. If you miss a day, skip it and keep going.

steps.name: Day 1: Read and copy
steps.text: Read the passage twice. Copy the one verse that stands out most at the top of the page.

steps.name: Day 2: Look for God
steps.text: Write what this passage shows about who God is. Look for words that describe Him or how He acts.

steps.name: Day 3: Look at the people
steps.text: Who is in the passage? What were they feeling or facing? Where do you see yourself in them?

steps.name: Day 4: Make it personal
steps.text: Write where this truth meets your life this week: a relationship, a worry, a decision or a habit.

steps.name: Day 5: Pray it back
steps.text: Turn the passage into a prayer. Use its words and ideas, then add your own.

steps.name: Day 6: Pray for others
steps.text: Who else needs this truth? Write their names and pray it for them.

steps.name: Day 7: Rest and remember
steps.text: Read your week's pages. Write one sentence you want to carry into next week.

blocks.h3: Passages that work well for a week

ul: Psalm 23
Proverbs 3:1-12
Isaiah 40:28-31
Matthew 6:25-34
Philippians 4:4-9
Colossians 3:12-17

blocks.p: Use these when the passage feels hard to start or you want a fresh angle. Write the prompt in the box called "Where this meets my life right now." For many more, see [Christian journal prompts for women](/christian-journal-prompts/).

ul: What does my quiet time look like right now, honestly? What would I like it to look like?
Which truth about God have I known for years but struggle to believe on hard days?
Where in this passage do I feel God's gentleness toward me?
What is God asking me to stop doing, and what is He asking me to start?
What did I pray for a year ago? How has He answered?
If I could ask God one question today, what would it be?
Which woman in the Bible do I relate to most this season, and why?
Where have I seen God's faithfulness in the last seven days?
What part of my life have I not invited Him into yet?
What would it look like to spend one hour with Jesus like Mary did?
What words do I use about myself that God would never use about me?
Where am I trying to earn love that is already given?
What am I comparing myself to lately, and how is it changing my mood?
What would I tell my younger self about how God sees her?
When did I last feel truly rested, and what made it different?
What fear has been making my choices for me this month?
Which strength has God given me that I tend to hide?
What do I need to forgive myself for, now that God has forgiven me?
What does beauty that comes from the inside look like in my daily life?
How can I treat my body this week as a gift from God?
Who needs my patience this week, and what makes it hard to give?
What prayer have I been praying for my family the longest?
Is there a friendship God is asking me to repair or to grow?
Who in my life is carrying something heavy without saying so?
How can I serve someone at home in a way they would notice?
Which older woman has shaped my faith? What did she teach me?
Which younger woman could I encourage this month?
Where do I need to set a kind but firm limit with someone?
What blessing would I speak over each person in my home tonight?
Whom have I been avoiding, and what would Jesus do?
What season of life am I in, and what is God teaching me in it?
Where am I serving out of love, and where out of guilt?
What dream have I set down that I want to talk to God about?
How can I honor God in my work this week, paid or unpaid?
What is one thing I can say no to so I can say yes to God?
What has this busy season taught me about my limits?
Where do I need wisdom for a decision this month?
What is God providing for me right now that I have overlooked?
How can my home, table or schedule bless someone outside my family?
What do I want people to remember about my faith one day?

example.label: Quiet time
example.title: Luke 10:38-42
example.text:
God here: Jesus is gentle with Martha. He is not angry.
My life: I am Martha this month. Lists, meals, work, no rest.
Today I will sit for ten minutes before I open my email.
Lord, I am tired. Teach me the one thing that is needed.
Gifts: a hug from Noah, a sunny window, leftovers for dinner.

blocks.p: Short and honest is the goal. More sample pages are in [prayer journal examples](/prayer-journal-examples/).

This same page works just as well for men. The method does not change: read, notice God, apply, pray. Men often like a shorter page with one clear action. Try writing only three lines: the verse, one thing it says, and one thing to do today.

ul: Where is God asking me to lead with humility this week?
What am I carrying alone that I should bring to God and a trusted friend?
How can I protect time with my family from work this week?
Where do I need courage to do what is right?
What does faithfulness look like in my job tomorrow?

blocks.p: For more, see the [prayer journal for men](/prayer-journal-for-men/).

sections.h2: Tips to keep your devotional journal going

ul: **Tie it to something you already do.** Morning coffee, the school run, lunch break or bedtime.
**Keep everything together.** Bible, pen and journal in one basket, or this page saved on your phone's home screen.
**Lower the bar.** One verse and one line is a win.
**Read with a friend.** Pick the same passage and text each other one thing you learned.
**Look back monthly.** Mark answered prayers and lessons you do not want to forget.

blocks.p: If you want a guided year, our Android app [Prayer Journal for Women](/prayer-journal-for-women/) gives you a Bible verse each week (KJV or WEB), the whole chapter, a reflection with three questions and a prayer page. faq.q: What is a devotional journal for women?
faq.a: It is a journal for a woman's daily or weekly quiet time with God. Each page has room for a Bible passage, what it shows about God, how it applies to her life, and a prayer. Many also include gratitude and a place for answered prayers.

faq.q: How do I start a devotional journal?
faq.a: Pick one short passage, like a psalm or a few verses from a gospel. Read it twice. Write the verse that stood out, what it shows about God, how it meets your life, and a short prayer. Do this for ten minutes a day. The free page above walks you through each step.

faq.q: What is a good devotional for women to start with?
faq.a: The Bible itself is the best place to start. Psalm 23, Luke 10:38-42, Proverbs 3 and Philippians 4 are gentle, clear passages. Spend a week on each one using the 7 day plan on this page before moving on.

faq.q: How much time should a devotional journal take?
faq.a: Ten minutes is a good target, but five is fine on busy days. What matters most is showing up regularly. Many women find a short daily time and a longer weekend time works well for their season.

faq.q: Can men use a devotional journal too?
faq.a: Yes. The method is the same for anyone: read, notice what it shows about God, apply it, and pray. Men often prefer a short three line page with one clear action for the day. The free template on this page works for men too.
